basic_details.scholarship_name: Geneva Academy Scholarships in International Humanitarian Law & Human Rights
basic_details.offering_entity: Geneva Academy of International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights (Joint Center of the University of Geneva & Geneva Graduate Institute - IHEID)
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: Geneva Academy of International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights (Villa Moynier, Geneva, Switzerland)
basic_details.major_restrictions: LL.M. in International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights (LL.M. IHL) and Master of Advanced Studies in Transitional Justice, Human Rights and the Rule of Law (MTJ).
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~15 to 20 full and partial scholarships awarded annually across both Master's programmes
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Open international competition with focus on candidates from developing and conflict-affected nations; typically 1 to 2 Pakistani legal scholars/advocates selected per intake
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: 10 months (full academic year from September to June covering the 1-year intensive Master's degree)

nationality_requirements: Open to international legal graduates and human rights advocates worldwide, with strong priority for candidates from non-Western/developing countries including Pakistan
eligibility_requirements.age_limit_notes: No rigid age ceiling; targeted at young legal practitioners, judicial officers, and civil society advocates under 40.
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: Full degree in law (LLB, BA-LLB 5-year, or equivalent recognized law degree) or another degree with significant legal coursework, from an HEC/Pakistan Bar Council-recognized university with high academic distinction (minimum CGPA 3.30 / 4.00 or 75%+).
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Minimum CGPA 3.30 / 4.00; competitive legal candidates typically hold CGPA >= 3.60 / 4.00 or rank in the top 10% of their law school class.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Recognized law degree (LLB) with solid background in public international law, constitutional law, human rights, or criminal law.
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Graduated with full primary law degree prior to commencement in September.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Practical experience in legal advocacy, judicial clerkships, human rights NGOs, ICRC/Red Crescent work, or moot court competitions is highly valued.
eligibility_requirements.language_notes: IELTS Academic minimum 7.0 (with no band below 6.5) or TOEFL iBT minimum 100. MOI certificates may be considered if previous law degree was conducted entirely in English.
eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: Instruction is in English (with bilingual optional courses in French for the LL.M.). Passive knowledge of French is advantageous but not mandatory.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: Full scholarships are reserved specifically for outstanding candidates from non-Western/developing countries who demonstrate that they cannot study in Geneva without financial support.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: Cannot hold another full institutional scholarship concurrently.

tuition_fee.details: 100% full tuition fee waiver for the intensive 10-month Master's programme (CHF 18,000 value).

admission_application_fee.details: Geneva Academy online application fee of CHF 100 payable during submission.

accommodation.details: Access to Geneva Graduate Institute student residences (Grand Morillon / Piccolo) or university housing; living stipend covers accommodation expenses.
accommodation.amount: Organized student residence access via living stipend

monthly_stipend.details: Monthly living allowance of CHF 1,800 per month for 10 months (~PKR 590,000 / month | CHF 18,000 total) to cover rent, meals, and living costs in Geneva.

airfare.details: International travel expenses between Pakistan and Geneva are self-funded or covered from personal savings.

visa_fee.details: Swiss student visa application fee and cantonal residence permit (Permis B) charges in Geneva (~CHF 200 - 300) covered by student.
visa_fee.amount: Swiss visa and cantonal permit fees borne by student

health_insurance.details: Contribution towards mandatory Swiss health and accident insurance (LAMal student policy) provided through the scholarship package.
health_insurance.amount: Swiss student health insurance contribution covered

food_allowance.details: Subsidized cafeterias at Villa Moynier, Graduate Institute, and Uni Mail; covered via monthly CHF 1,800 living stipend.

books_and_materials_allowance.details: Full access to the Geneva Academy Library, Graduate Institute Kathryn and Shelby Cullom Davis Library, and UN Library Geneva.
books_and_materials_allowance.amount: Full access to specialized UN & Academy libraries

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Participation in study trips to international courts and tribunals in The Hague, Strasbourg, or Paris, and UN briefings in Geneva.
research_funding_conference_grant.amount: Study trips to international courts included

travel_transit_allowance.details: Subsidized Geneva public transit (Unireso / tpg monthly student pass).

university_and_program_options.single_or_multiple_universities: Single specialized joint institution (Geneva Academy of International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights, Geneva, Switzerland).
participating_institutions: Geneva Academy of International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights
university_and_program_options.university_rankings_scope: World's foremost center of excellence in international humanitarian law, human rights, and armed conflict studies; located at the global epicenter of multilateral diplomacy.
available_majors: LL.M. in International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights
Master of Advanced Studies in Transitional Justice, Human Rights and the Rule of Law (MTJ)
Executive Master in International Law in Armed Conflict
university_and_program_options.admission_requirements_summary: Law degree (LLB / 5-year BA-LLB) with CGPA >= 3.30/4.00, demonstrated commitment to humanitarian law/human rights, IELTS 7.0+ or TOEFL 100+ / law MOI, two recommendation letters, and completed online application with financial request.
university_and_program_options.easiest_hardest_institutions_guidance: Single integrated application: applicants request scholarship consideration directly within the online application form before the January deadline.
university_and_program_options.strategic_program_match_advice: Highlight practical commitment to human rights advocacy, public international law, or transitional justice issues in Pakistan and explain how Geneva training will empower your legal practice.

application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the Geneva Academy application portal, select chosen Master's programme, tick the box requesting a scholarship, complete all personal/academic sections, upload required legal credentials, and submit before late January.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Check eligibility criteria and review curriculum for the LL.M. or MTJ programme.
Step 2: Create an account on the Geneva Academy online admissions portal.
Step 3: Fill in biographical, academic, and professional experience sections.
Step 4: Check the box indicating request for a full or partial scholarship.
Step 5: Upload your motivation letter explaining both academic interest and financial circumstances.
Step 6: Upload LLB degree certificate, transcripts, CV, and two letters of recommendation.
Step 7: Upload household income documentation demonstrating financial need.
Step 8: Pay the CHF 100 application fee and submit the application before January 27.
Step 9: Selection committee reviews applications and communicates decisions in March/April.
Step 10: Confirm scholarship acceptance and apply for the Swiss entry visa.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Combined Integrated Application: The scholarship request is submitted simultaneously within the Master's admission application form.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted either directly as signed PDF uploads by the applicant or sent via referee contact details according to portal instructions.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Detailed motivation statement outlining: (1) Academic and professional interest in international humanitarian law and human rights, (2) Relevant legal experience, (3) Career aspirations upon return, (4) Specific reasons for requiring financial assistance.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Brief statement of legal topics of particular interest for the Master's paper/dissertation.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Standard legal CV detailing education, moot court competitions, legal publications, internships, and bar admissions.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: No interview; selections are based entirely on academic transcripts, legal credentials, motivation letter, and references.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic minimum 7.0 or TOEFL iBT minimum 100 / verified law degree MOI.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: HEC and MOFA degree attestation required for Pakistani applicants prior to visa processing.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Official English or French translation of all non-English academic documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: Online submission via the Geneva Academy application portal.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Official law degree certificate from an HEC/Pakistan Bar Council-recognized law faculty.
Complete law school transcripts detailing all subjects, grades, and CGPA (minimum 3.30 / 4.00).
Legal CV highlighting bar admissions, litigation/advocacy experience, moot courts, and research.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Highlight human rights advocacy or legal aid work.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Comprehensive statement explaining passion for IHL/human rights, professional goals, and financial need.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Articulate how Geneva training will contribute to the legal system in Pakistan.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Confidential reference letters on official letterhead from law professors or legal supervisors.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Signed and stamped on official institutional letterhead.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Official documentation verifying household financial situation (tax returns, bank statements, salary slips).
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Clear documentation establishing inability to self-fund Swiss living costs.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Official IELTS (min 7.0), TOEFL iBT (min 100), or official university Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Valid test score or official law school MOI letter.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Clear scan of valid international passport.

important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Scholarship applications strictly close January 27; self-funded applications accepted until late February.

selection_process_and_weights.academic_weight: 40% (Academic excellence in law studies and university ranking)
selection_process_and_weights.extracurricular_and_leadership_weight: 15% (Moot court competitions, human rights advocacy, legal aid initiatives)
selection_process_and_weights.research_experience_weight: 15% (Law review publications, legal dissertations, and analytical legal writing)
selection_process_and_weights.work_experience_weight: 10% (Legal practice, judicial clerkships, or NGO human rights advocacy)
selection_process_and_weights.personal_statement_weight: 20% (Quality, articulation, and persuasive dedication in the motivation statement)
selection_process_and_weights.financial_need_weight: 0% (Qualifying prerequisite: candidate must demonstrate financial need)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: Geneva Academy Admissions and Scholarships Committee comprising resident professors and academic directors.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Rigorous holistic assessment scoring academic rigor, professional dedication to human rights, and potential for leadership in international law.

competitiveness_profile.total_annual_applicants: ~600 to 900 international legal graduates and human rights advocates apply annually
competitiveness_profile.total_scholarships_awarded: ~15 to 20 full and partial scholarships awarded per intake
competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_pakistan: ~4% to 6% among high-achieving law graduates with human rights track records
competitiveness_profile.typical_successful_applicant_gpa: 3.65 / 4.00 with demonstrated practical legal experience or moot court honors
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Law graduates (LLB) with distinguished records in human rights advocacy, judicial clerkships, or international legal research.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Graduates from LUMS (Shaikh Ahmad Hassan School of Law), Quaid-i-Azam University, University of London International Programmes in Pakistan, and Punjab University Law College.
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: Pakistan, Colombia, Kenya, Palestine, Ukraine, India, Nigeria, Lebanon, Myanmar.

fake_websites_and_scams: Only apply via the official Geneva Academy portal at https://www.geneva-academy.ch/.
Beware of unauthorized agents claiming to secure Swiss visa or scholarship placements.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: The Geneva Academy charges a standard CHF 100 application fee for processing admission and scholarship requests.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: Applications submitted through educational agencies or consultants are strictly disregarded.
hidden_costs_breakdown: Swiss student visa and cantonal residence permit fees in Geneva: ~CHF 250 - 350 (~PKR 80,000 - 110,000).
Tuition (CHF 18,000) and monthly living stipend (CHF 1,800/mo) are fully covered by the scholarship.
misleading_claims_debunked: Myth: You must be fluent in French to apply. Reality: The LL.M. and MTJ programmes are taught 100% in English (French is optional).
Myth: Only licensed courtroom litigators can apply. Reality: Recent law graduates with strong academic credentials and NGO or moot court experience are regularly awarded full scholarships.
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Unofficial websites frequently suggest that scholarship applications can be submitted after receiving admission; at Geneva Academy, scholarship requests must be submitted together with the admission file before January 27.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Must pass all coursework assessments, moot court exercises, and complete the LL.M. / MTJ Master's paper.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Mandatory full-time attendance on campus at Villa Moynier in Geneva.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Term-by-term assessment monitoring by the Board of Studies.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Part-time work in Switzerland is highly restricted during the 10-month intensive programme and not recommended.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: Scholars are strongly expected to return to their home countries or work in international human rights institutions to advance international law.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.service_obligations_or_bonds: Commitment to upholding and advancing human rights and international humanitarian principles.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Revocation of remaining scholarship installments if student withdraws without justification or breaches academic conduct.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Course transfers between LL.M. and MTJ programmes are generally not permitted after matriculation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Strictly limited to the 10-month duration of the Master's programme; no scholarship extension possible.
